authorInfo.bio: Daniel Defoe was an English writer, journalist, merchant and spy. He is famous for his novels Robinson Crusoe (1719), Moll Flanders (1722), Colonel Jack (1722), and Roxana: The Fortunate Mistress (1724). He has been seen as one of the earliest proponents of the English novel, and helped to popularise the form in Britain with others such as Aphra Behn and Samuel Richardson.

description: "Atalantis Major" by Daniel Defoe is a political allegory written in the early 18th century, particularly around the time of the Tory victory in the 1710 election in Great Britain. The book serves as a satirical commentary on the political turmoil of Defoe's time, focusing on issues related to the election of Scottish peers and the delicate landscape of party allegiance during Queen Anne's reign.
